title: Ore Reserve and Resource Assessment
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/metals-mining/01 - Ore Reserve and Resource Assessment.md
goal: The goal of this analysis is to evaluate the quantity, quality, and economic viability of a mining company’s ore reserves and resources.
dataRequired: Geological survey reports and maps.
Drilling and sampling data (e.g., grade, tonnage).
Reserve and resource classification (Measured, Indicated, Inferred).
Metallurgical recovery rates.
Commodity price forecasts.
Operational cost estimates (mining, processing, logistics).
Regulatory and environmental compliance data.
improve: Conduct additional drilling and sampling programs to increase reserve confidence levels.
Invest in advanced geological modeling tools to improve resource estimation accuracy.
Reassess cut-off grades to optimize economic extraction under varying market conditions.
Collaborate with metallurgical experts to enhance recovery rates through improved processing techniques.
Regularly update resource and reserve models to reflect changes in commodity prices and operational costs.

formulas.source: Cut-off Grade = Operating Costs / (Commodity Price x Recovery Rate).

title: Reserve Replacement Rate and Resource Conversion Analysis
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/metals-mining/02 - Reserve Replacement Rate and Resource Conversion Analysis.md
goal: The goal of this analysis is to assess a mining company’s ability to replace depleted reserves through exploration, development, or acquisitions and to evaluate the effectiveness of converting resources into economically viable reserves.
dataRequired: Annual production data (ore quantity and grade extracted).
Reserve additions (through exploration, development, or acquisitions).
Resource-to-reserve conversion data (historical and projected).
Exploration expenditures and results.
Resource classification data (Measured, Indicated, Inferred).
Reserve and resource reporting standards (e.g., JORC, NI 43-101).
improve: Prioritize high-potential exploration targets using advanced geophysical and geochemical techniques.
Increase investment in brownfield projects near existing operations for lower-risk reserve additions.
Strengthen resource modeling and mine planning to improve resource-to-reserve conversion rates.
Form strategic partnerships or acquisitions to access additional reserves.
Enhance exploration efficiency by adopting innovative drilling and sampling technologies.
Regularly update exploration and development strategies based on market conditions and geological insights.

formulas.source: RRR = (Reserves Added / Reserves Depleted) x 100
Resource Conversion Rate = (Reserves Added from Resource Conversion / Total Measured and Indicated Resources) x 100
Discovery Cost = Exploration Expenditures / Reserves Added

title: Exploration and Development Pipeline Review
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/metals-mining/03 - Exploration and Development Pipeline Review.md

Exploration results (e.g., drilling data, sampling reports).
Development timelines and milestones.

Historical success rates for exploration projects.

improve: Regularly review and update the exploration and development pipeline to prioritize high-potential projects.
Increase collaboration between geologists, engineers, and financial teams to optimize resource allocation.
Strengthen stakeholder engagement to address community or regulatory challenges early in the project lifecycle.
Adopt advanced exploration technologies (e.g., AI for geospatial analysis) to improve success rates.
Develop contingency plans for high-risk projects to minimize potential disruptions.
Monitor competitor pipelines to identify gaps or opportunities in the company’s strategy.

title: Exploration Success Rate and Discovery Cost Analysis
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/metals-mining/04 - Exploration Success Rate and Discovery Cost Analysis.md
goal: The goal of this analysis is to evaluate the effectiveness and efficiency of a mining company’s exploration activities by measuring the rate of successful discoveries and the cost per unit of discovered resources.
dataRequired: Total number of exploration projects undertaken in the analysis period.
Number of projects that resulted in economically viable discoveries.
Exploration expenditures (e.g., drilling, sampling, surveying).
Total quantity of resources discovered (e.g., in tons, ounces, or carats).
Classification of discoveries (Measured, Indicated, Inferred).
improve: Use advanced geophysical and geochemical techniques to improve targeting accuracy.

formulas.source: Success Rate (%) = (Number of Successful Discoveries / Total Number of Projects) x 100
Discovery Cost ($/unit) = Total Exploration Expenditures / Total Quantity of

title: Stripping Ratio and Waste-to-Ore Ratio Evaluation
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/metals-mining/05 - Stripping Ratio and Waste-to-Ore Ratio Evaluation.md
goal: The goal of this analysis is to assess the ratio of waste material to ore extracted in mining operations.
dataRequired: Total volume or weight of waste material removed (e.g., in cubic meters or tons).
Total volume or weight of ore extracted (e.g., in tons).
Historical stripping ratios and waste-to-ore ratios for benchmarking.
Cost data for waste removal and ore extraction.
Geotechnical and mine design data for assessing overburden thickness and ore body geometry.
improve: Optimize mine design and pit geometry to reduce waste removal.
Use selective mining techniques to minimize waste extraction while maximizing ore recovery.
Invest in advanced geotechnical analysis to identify efficient access points for ore bodies.
Reevaluate cut-off grades to focus on higher-grade ore, reducing waste-to-ore ratios.
Explore technological solutions like in-pit crushing and conveying (IPCC) to reduce waste handling costs.
Develop waste management plans to minimize environmental impact and enhance land reclamation efforts.

variables: Volume or Weight of Waste Removed
Volume or Weight of Ore Extracted
formulas.source: Stripping Ratio = (Volume or Weight of Waste Removed / Volume or Weight of Ore Extracted)
Waste-to-Ore Ratio = (Weight of Waste Removed / Weight of Ore Extracted)

variables: Cost per Unit of Waste Removal
formulas.source: Cost Impact = (Waste Quantity x Cost per Unit of Waste Removal).

formulas.source: Recovery Rate (%) = (Recovered Metal / Contained Metal in Ore) x 100
Recoverable Value = (Grade x Recovery Rate x Commodity Price).

sourcePath: data/analysis-library/metals-mining/09 - Mine Life and Production Capacity Evaluation.md

formulas.source: Operating Cost per Unit ($/unit) = Total Operating Costs / Total Units of
formulas.step: Calculate Total Operating Cost per Unit

title: Operational Efficiency and Throughput Analysis
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/metals-mining/11 - Operational Efficiency and Throughput Analysis.md
goal: The goal of this analysis is to evaluate the efficiency of mining operations and the throughput capacity of processing plants.
dataRequired: Daily, monthly, and annual production data (ore processed and metal/mineral produced).
Equipment utilization rates and downtime records.
Processing plant throughput capacity (tons per hour or day).
Labor productivity metrics (output per worker).
Energy and material consumption rates.
Maintenance schedules and costs.
Benchmark data for similar operations or industry averages.
improve: Implement predictive maintenance systems to minimize unplanned equipment downtime.
Optimize workflows by addressing bottlenecks in hauling, crushing, or processing operations.

formulas.source: Equipment Utilization (%) = (Operating Hours / Total Available Hours) x 100
Throughput Efficiency (%) = (Actual Throughput / Design Throughput) x 100
Labor Productivity = Total Output / Number of Workers

title: Mining Equipment and Maintenance Efficiency Review
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/metals-mining/12 - Mining Equipment and Maintenance Efficiency Review.md
goal: The goal of this analysis is to evaluate the performance and maintenance efficiency of mining equipment to minimize downtime, reduce operating costs, and improve productivity.
dataRequired: Equipment inventory and specifications (make, model, capacity, age).
Equipment utilization data (operating hours, idle hours, and downtime).
**Maintenance records (frequency, cost, and type of maintenance:** preventive, corrective, predictive).
Operational performance metrics (e.g., tons moved, processed, or hauled per hour).
Fuel and energy consumption rates.
Benchmark data for similar equipment in comparable operations.
improve: Transition to predictive maintenance systems using IoT and AI to anticipate failures and reduce unplanned downtime.
Implement operator training programs to minimize equipment misuse or overloading.
Optimize maintenance schedules to balance preventive care and equipment availability.
Upgrade or replace aging equipment with newer, more efficient models.

formulas.source: Utilization (%) = (Operating Hours / Total Available Hours) x 100
MTBF = Total Operating Time / Number of Failures
MTTR = Total Downtime / Number of Repairs
Equipment Productivity = (Tons Moved or Processed / Operating Hours).

title: Grade Control and Dilution Management Analysis
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/metals-mining/15 - Grade Control and Dilution Management Analysis.md
goal: The goal of this analysis is to evaluate and optimize grade control practices to minimize ore dilution and maximize ore recovery.
dataRequired: Geological models and block models of the ore deposit.
Ore and waste boundaries (planned vs. actual).

Production data (ore tonnage, waste tonnage, grade delivered to the plant).

formulas.source: Dilution (%) = (Tonnage of Diluted Material / Total Ore Tonnage) x 100
Ore Recovery (%) = (Ore Tonnage Recovered / Planned Ore Tonnage) x 100
Cost Impact ($) = (Diluted Material x Mining Cost per Ton) + (Lost Grade x Processing Cost per Unit).
